title: Granular ingress/egress microtiers + standing commit trial and SQ implications
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Background:
Redwood has multiple hosted customers pushing high-bandwidth streaming workloads and synchronous batch generation. Current per-token metering conflates ingress (input tokens) and egress (output tokens) into a single rate in many proposals, which obscures cost drivers for prompt-heavy vs. generation-heavy workloads. Enterprise buyers request clearer line items on contracts and are asking for per-direction accounting in security questionnaires and procurement reviews.

Objective:
Design and trial a microtiered per-token pricing model that separates ingress vs egress rates, introduces small standing-commit discounts (monthly), and tests a low-friction minimum-billing reconciliation mechanism for legacy enterprise contracting. Measure revenue, churn signal, and operational complexity. Produce a guidance doc for Sales and Security when answering enterprise SQs referencing pricing granularity and reconciliation rules.

Hypotheses:
1) Separating ingress vs egress rates will reduce sticker shock for prompt-heavy customers without materially reducing revenue from generation-heavy customers because standing commit discounts will be targeted.
2) Small standing commits (e.g., $2k/mo equivalent) will increase revenue predictability and reduce churn for customers doing >100M tokens/mo.
3) A reconciliation flow that credits overage versus committed minimums on a trailing-month basis will be simpler to implement and acceptable to procurement/legal.

Experiment design (A/B cohort over 8 weeks):
- Control: current unified per-token rate (baseline).
- Variant A: microtiers: ingress rate = baseline * 0.7, egress rate = baseline * 1.25; three microtiers defined at token thresholds {0-10M, 10M-100M, 100M+} with progressively larger standing-commit discounts.
- Variant B: same directional rates as A but with optional standing commit product (three bands) and a "reconciliation credit" for unused committed tokens applied monthly.
- Eligibility: self-serve hosted accounts and Sales-identified enterprise pilot customers (opt-in).

Telemetry & success metrics:
- Primary: delta in ARR from cohort vs control, and net revenue retention for pilot customers at 90 days.
- Secondary: % of customers opting into standing commits, change in average invoice size, percent of tokens billed as ingress vs egress, number of billing disputes opened.
- Operational: implementation effort (ENG story points), new invoice fields added, accounting treatment notes for Finance.

Billing & implementation notes for ENG/Finance:
- Metering: extend current token metering to label token direction at ingestion-stage. This must be reflected in aggregated usage rows (no per-request line-items required for self-serve).
- Reconciliation: implement a monthly credit where committed quantity is compared to observed usage and credit applied to next invoice as a negative line item.
- Back-compat: customers not opted in see unchanged invoices and no new line items.
- Fraud/cost risk: streaming connections can be long-lived. Add sampling checks for synthetic token inflation and rate-limit guardrails.

Security Questionnaire (SQ) & Contracting guidance:
- We will author an SQ appendix that explains: how usage is metered, where tokens are logged, retention of metering telemetry (30 days by default, extendable), and how standing commitments appear in contract exhibits.
- Provide standard contract language samples for Sales: (a) definition of ingress/egress tokens, (b) reconciliation clause, (c) audit window and data required for invoice disputes.

Risks & trade-offs:
- Complexity for customers who use both heavy prompts and heavy generations; UI must clearly display direction split in Console.
- Revenue leakage risk if egress rate is set too low; mitigation is to start with conservative uplift and test elasticity.
- Legal/Finance needs to sign off on reconciliation credit flow to ensure ASC/GAAP alignment.

Next steps & timeline:
- Week 0-1: finalize microtier thresholds and discount bands (PM + Finance).
- Week 2-3: ENG scope: metering label + billing line-item prototype (ENG-21456).
- Week 4: Sales pilot onboarding + Sales enablement doc.
- Week 5-8: Run experiment; weekly metric reviews.
- Week 9: Post-mortem and decision on roll-forward.
